key_insight: A proposed photonic Maxwell’s demon admits sunlight and traps wavelength-converted radiation, enabling photon recycling for solar heat storage and thermophotovoltaics.
engineering_relevance: Spectrally selective enclosures could improve optical utilization in solar thermal systems and ultra-low-bandgap photovoltaic devices.
method: Use multilayer dielectric mirrors that transmit incoming wavelengths but reflect longer wavelengths.
Place an irreversible wavelength converter or blackbody behind the mirrors inside a 3D enclosure.
Recycle trapped radiation, optionally coupling it to an internal ultra-low-bandgap photovoltaic cell.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical proposal, citing the 93.3% Landsberg limit as an ideal benchmark rather than a demonstrated device efficiency.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on broadband, angle-tolerant spectral selectivity and low parasitic losses; near-complete optical utilization does not guarantee comparable electrical efficiency.
paper_title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
